abstract: The Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK) has been conducting research on the development of advanced terrestrial broadcasting technology to transmit ultrahigh-definition television (UHDTV) signals. To analyze the transmission characteristics of the proposed system, we designed a prototype modulator and demodulator, and measured their performance through laboratory experiments. Further, we also evaluated the proposed system via large-scale field trials under conditions similar to actual broadcast propagation environments. This paper presents the concept and specifications of the proposed system. The verification results of a computer simulation, and laboratory and large-scale field experiments are also described.

authors.bio: Noriyuki Shirai received BE and ME degrees in electrical engineering from the Tokyo University of Science, Chiba, Japan. He joined Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Tokyo, Japan, in 2004. Since 2013, he has been working for NHK Science and Technology Research Laboratories (STRL). He is a research engineer for the Advanced Transmission Systems Research Division and is engaged in the development of next-generation terrestrial broadcasting systems for ultrahigh definition television (UHDTV). He is a member of the Institute of Image Information and Television Engineers (ITE).

authors.bio: Madoka Nakamura received BE and ME degrees in electric engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, Japan, in 1998 and 2000, respectively. She joined NHK in 2000. authors.bio: Masayuki Takada received a BE degree in communication engineering and an ME degree in electronic engineering from Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan, in 1986 and 1988, respectively. He joined NHK in 1988 and has been working in the NHK STRL. Currently, he is the head of the Advanced Transmission Systems Research Division with NHK STRL. He was engaged in the development of broadcasting systems, especially FM subcarrier systems, DTTB systems, the next-generation ISDB-T system, and UHDTV satellite broadcasting. He is also active in the standardization of broadcast technologies in Association of Radio Industries and Businesses (ARIB). He is a member of ITE and IEICE in Japan, and a member of IEEE.
